constraints.authenticity_dispute: a long comment thread (comments 9-27, Aug 2017) argues the document is a forgery: the rank-stamp eagle faces the wrong direction for a genuine Reichsadler stamp of the period, 'Lublin' is misspelled on the stamp ('Cztl.' for 'Kztl.'), Fraktur-s usage is inconsistent, the sender's unit (10. SS-Panzer-Division, stationed in France Feb 1944) does not match the stamp's origin (Lublin concentration camp, eastern Poland), rank abbreviations are non-standard (StdF instead of Staf; capital F instead of lowercase f), and a near-identical forged 'Funkspruch' was later sold on eBay by a named dealer (comment 28, 31 May 2021) -- UNSOLVED-SURVEY.md's row already records 'Bourdeau: probable forgery (typography, rank abbreviations)', consistent with this thread
constraints.unusual_form: Schmeh: none of the WW2 encryption methods he knows produce ciphertexts with this internal =, /, : punctuation -- worth comparing against the standard German WW2 Wehrmacht/SS Spruchformular layout (a successor form existed from May 1941, per commenter Thomas, cryptomuseum.com/crypto/enigma/forms) once transcribed, since the punctuation may mark form fields (addressee/date/serial) rather than cipher structure
